description: workflow/04a_multiclass_selection.smk: screening of the candidates for the multiclass data set of experiment C by the criteria of docs/experiment_plan.md, section 5d (fixed in commit a4b5f17, before any candidate file was downloaded). E1, E2 and P1 are documentary: they are stated here with the evidence read on 'verified'; E3-E8 and P2 are computed by python/sharedimp_exp/multiclass_selection.py from the downloaded files (pinned by sha256). E9 belongs to workflow 04 (it needs the R and Python jobs). Criteria are assessed in order; after the first failure the later ones are not assessed. No importance is computed here.
license_evidence: each landing page carries the link 'Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)'; DOI, creators, number of instances and of features come from the UCI API (https://archive.ics.uci.edu/api/dataset?id=<id>)

abalone.title: Abalone, Sex (M, F, I) as response

E1.evidence: stable CSV URL, DOI 10.24432/C55C7W, CC BY 4.0 on the landing page

E2.evidence: three levels of Sex (M, F, I = infant); a row is one abalone of the field study of Nash et al. (1994), Sea Fisheries Division Technical Report 48 (abalone.names: 'Number of Instances: 4177'; examples with missing values were removed by the donor)

P1.evidence: the documented purpose is predicting the number of rings (age); Sex is documented as a nominal attribute, not as a target. A web search on 2026-11-14 found tutorials but no publication to cite for Sex as the response; the uses listed in abalone.names classify ring groups
